reasoning: Recent high-quality public polling over the last month consistently shows Democrat Roy Cooper leading Republican Michael Whatley in the 2026 North Carolina Senate race by mid- to high-single digits, with one reputable aggregate putting the race around D+8 and an individual Fox News poll at D+9.[1][4][5][6] A newer Public Policy Polling survey within the same window shows a tighter D+4 margin, but this appears to be an outlier relative to the aggregate and the larger-sample Fox News poll, so the best current estimate is that the Senate race stands roughly at **D+7–8** statewide, despite North Carolina’s underlying R+3 Cook PVI.[1][2][4][5][6]

sources.name: PollsMax
sources.details: PollsMax polling average for the 2026 North Carolina Senate race shows Roy Cooper 48.5% and Michael Whatley 40.5%, an overall margin of D+7.9 based on 20 polls.

sources.name: WFAE (reporting Public Policy Polling)
sources.details: Public Policy Polling survey of 759 North Carolina voters finds Cooper leading Whatley 48% to 44%, a D+4 margin, indicating the race has tightened compared to earlier in the year.

sources.name: Asheville Citizen-Times (reporting Public Policy Polling)
sources.details: Citizen-Times report on the same PPP poll shows Cooper at 48% and Whatley at 44%, a D+4 margin, with note that this is similar to PPP’s March findings.

sources.name: Fox News Poll (Beacon Research/Shaw & Company Research)
sources.details: Fox News Poll of 1,005 registered voters in North Carolina finds Cooper leading Whatley 53% to 44%, a D+9 margin statewide, with even larger leads among highly interested or motivated voters.

sources.name: WTVD/ABC11 (reporting Fox News poll)
sources.details: WTVD/ABC11 summary of the Fox News poll reports Cooper ahead of Whatley 53% to 44%, confirming a D+9 margin in the North Carolina Senate race.

sources.name: Yahoo News (reporting Fox News poll)
sources.details: Yahoo News write-up of the Fox News poll reiterates Cooper at 53% and Whatley at 44%, a D+9 margin, describing Cooper’s lead as significant as the race "kicks into full gear."
